hypothesis: Test symmetric boosted trees with a larger fixed capacity budget, ordered residual estimation and Langevin regularization. These change the fitting mechanism relative to the completed HGB/XGBoost families. The primary literature motivates possible improvements, not an expected gain on this dependent market dataset.
partition: Exactly the original four historical days d-5 through d-2 at the original calendar stride of four seconds. Preserve every original 7070 noon assessment row per asset/date. All historical label release clocks must precede assessment. No assessment or previous-noon outcome enters fitting or iteration selection; all variants use a fixed final tree count.
preprocessing: Use the original raw observed feature columns. Fit pooled .001/.999 quantile clipping on historical training rows only, matching the HGB/XGBoost convention, then append the numeric 0/1 asset indicator and use float32. Keep every original column. No categorical target encoding, clock feature, query-time normalization or source selection.
chronological_order: Sort the full historical pool by decision timestamp, breaking equal-time ties by asset ID (BTC before ETH). Supply this order and timestamp metadata with has_time=true. Timestamp is not a model feature. This controls ordering inside the historical fit; it does not claim that an outcome is available to an online learner immediately at its historical decision time, or that adjacent overlapping labels are independent.
loss_and_priors: Native MultiClass loss on class indices 0/1/2 corresponding to -1/0/+1. Give each training row weight N/(6*n[asset,class]); no additional native class-weight multiplier. Return natural-probability p proportional to native q times the exact historical per-asset class prior. This is the existing ideal prior-recovery convention, not proof of calibration.
ordered_options: Use native Ordered mode with fold_len_multiplier=2 and approx_on_full_history=false. Record effective native parameters after fitting. Do not equate ordering within historical training with an independent-data guarantee; the market rows and their five-second labels remain temporally dependent.
langevin_options: Use the native posterior_sampling configuration, which enables Langevin mode, diffusion_temperature=N and model_shrink_rate=1/(2*N). Verify these effective values on the pinned runtime. This is a composite noise/shrinkage intervention, not an isolated noise ablation. Nominal N is the training row count, not the effective number of independent observations. No posterior uncertainty, mixing, global-optimum or finite-sample generalization claim is made from one finite run.
fixed_tree_count_reason: A shrinking boosted model changes earlier-tree contributions as it trains. A truncated prefix of the final model is not assumed identical to an earlier training checkpoint. All four variants therefore use exactly the final 1000-tree model, without staged-prefix selection or early stopping.
capacity_scope: Symmetric depth-six/eight trees differ from HGB and XGBoost in split sharing, leaf structure, regularization and compute. Report the within-CatBoost plain6/ordered6/langevin6 comparisons separately. Do not claim cross-library capacity equivalence. min_data_in_leaf is deliberately not set: it is not a supported regularizer for SymmetricTree growth.
fixed_blends: Average each of eight new sources 50/50 with its representation's original neural model and with deep500_hgb, giving sixteen blends. Retain all 208 completed retrieval-family sources. No blend-weight search.
runtime: CatBoost 1.2.10 official CPython 3.12 macOS universal2 wheel, SHA256 b27115d5b443048f710001c8ac666892dfe03498492310b00466203c91cc30a5, 28884278 bytes. Install into a separate research runtime; preserve the existing NumPy/sklearn/Torch environment and all running-study hashes. No GPU, paid compute or external account is needed.
preflight: After the current retrieval study finishes, run separately frozen synthetic native-runtime checks for all four variants at both 221 and 400 input dimensions. Verify probability/label order, effective ordered and Langevin settings, row/prefix independence, class-weight/prior semantics and exact native checkpoint forecasts. Measure bounded full-row-count fits and project the 1000-tree cost using a prospectively specified rule. Pin all source, wheel and runtime hashes, record limits and failed attempts, and do not resize or relax a failure implicitly.
assessment: Complete the entire three-date family before opening assessment scores. Preserve original rows, labels, timestamps, priors and retained forecasts. Report mean, asset and date effects against both matched mechanisms and the strongest retained complete procedure. These exposed dates cannot establish the substantial independent-gain gate.

primary_sources.scope: Ordered boosting motivates changing residual estimation. The theoretical setting and tabular benchmarks do not prove unbiasedness or an accuracy gain for dependent crypto labels.
SGLB, ICML 2021, motivates Langevin noise and shrinkage in boosting. Our finite multiclass run is not a replication of its asymptotic guarantees or its 0-1-loss experiments.

Official parameter semantics: CPU Ordered/MultiClass and Langevin support, chronological has_time, symmetric-tree limitations, and the three posterior_sampling settings. Check the actual pinned implementation as well.
Official version, compatible wheel and checksum provenance.
